question: In a Texas child-care center licensed for 13 or more children, with 13 or more children in care, what is the maximum number of children one caregiver may supervise when the specified age of the children in the group is 0–11 months?
quote: The classroom ratio is the number of children one caregiver may supervise and is shown in the following chart. ... Then the maximum number of children one caregiver may supervise is… 0 – 11 months 4
notes: Youngest band in the chart. 12-17 months is 1:5. The 'specified age' is the age of the middle child when the group is listed youngest to oldest (§746.1603). Centers with 12 or fewer children in care use a different mixed-age chart (Division 3, §746.1701).

question: In a Texas child-care center licensed for 13 or more children, with 13 or more children in care, what is the maximum number of children one caregiver may supervise when the specified age of the children in the group is 3 years?
quote: The classroom ratio is the number of children one caregiver may supervise and is shown in the following chart. ... Then the maximum number of children one caregiver may supervise is… 3 years 15
notes: Specified age = age of the middle child in the group (§746.1603). Maximum group size for 3 years is 30 (§746.1609). Centers with 12 or fewer children in care follow Division 3 (§746.1701).

question: In a Texas child-care center licensed for 13 or more children, with 13 or more children in care, what is the maximum number of children one caregiver may supervise when the specified age of the children in the group is 4 years?
quote: The classroom ratio is the number of children one caregiver may supervise and is shown in the following chart. ... Then the maximum number of children one caregiver may supervise is… 4 years 18
notes: Specified age = age of the middle child in the group (§746.1603). Opening/closing exception allows 1:16 for children 18 months and older (§746.1615); naptime ratio may be reduced 50% under conditions (§746.1613).

question: In a Texas child-care center licensed for 13 or more children, with 13 or more children in care, what is the maximum number of children one caregiver may supervise when the specified age of the children in the group is 9–13 years?
quote: The classroom ratio is the number of children one caregiver may supervise and is shown in the following chart. ... Then the maximum number of children one caregiver may supervise is… 9-13 years 26
notes: Oldest school-age band. The 6-8 years band is also 26. Field trips mixing with the public use a stricter chart (1:12 for 6 years and older, §746.1801).

question: In a Texas child-care center licensed for 13 or more children, with 13 or more children in care, what is the maximum group size when the specified age of the children in the group is 4 years?
quote: The maximum group size and the number of children two or more caregivers may supervise when 13 or more children are in care is specified in the following chart ... 4 years 35
notes: Group size may be exceeded for joint activities for up to 30 minutes for children 18 months through four years, and for meals, field trips, outdoor play and naptime (§746.1611). With 12 or fewer children in care the maximum group size is 12 (§746.1705).

question: Under Texas's Minimum Standards for Child-Care Centers, what minimum age must a caregiver at a licensed child-care center in Texas meet under the general caregiver qualifications?
quote: each caregiver must comply with minimum standards for employees and must [Low]: (1) Be at least 18 years of age
notes: Exceptions: a 16 or 17 year old with a high school diploma or equivalent, or a 16-18 year old still in high school, may be counted in ratio if never left alone with sole responsibility, supervised in the same room by a qualified caregiver, and in/through an approved child-care career program (§746.1109).

question: In Texas, besides one of the listed education-and-experience combinations, what minimum age and baseline education must the director of a child-care center licensed for 13 or more children have?
answer: At least 21 years of age and a high school diploma or its equivalent
quote: the director of a child-care center licensed for 13 or more children must be at least 21 years of age, have a high school diploma or its equivalent, and meet one of the following combinations of education and experience
notes: Figure: 26 TAC §746.1015 lists the combinations, e.g. a bachelor degree with 12 college credit hours in child development and six in management plus one year of experience in a licensed child-care center. Directors of centers licensed for 12 or fewer children: also at least 21 with a high school diploma, but different combinations (§746.1017).

question: How many clock hours of annual training must each caregiver at a licensed child-care center in Texas complete?
quote: 24 clock hours of annual training as required by §746.1309 of this division (relating to What areas of training must the annual training for caregivers cover?). (B) Each caregiver.
notes: Due within 12 months of employment and during each 12-month period after (Figure: 26 TAC §746.1301(a)). The director needs 30 clock hours (§746.1311). At least six hours must be in child growth and development topics (§746.1309(b)).

question: How many square feet of indoor activity space per child must a licensed child-care center in Texas have?
unit: square feet per child (based on licensed capacity)
quote: You must have at least 30 square feet of indoor activity space for each child that you are licensed to serve
notes: Measured per child the center is licensed to serve. Kindergarten/nursery schools and schools licensed before September 1, 2003 need only 20 square feet per child while that permit remains valid (§746.4207).

question: How many square feet of outdoor activity space must a licensed child-care center in Texas provide for each child using the outdoor activity area at one time?
unit: square feet per child using the area at one time
quote: You must have 80 square feet of outdoor activity space for each child using the outdoor activity area at one time
notes: Per child using the area at one time, not per licensed capacity. The outdoor space must also hold at least 25% of licensed indoor capacity (§746.4301(b)). Alternate care and get-well care programs are excepted.

question: If hot water is accessible to children at a licensed child-care center in Texas, what is the maximum water temperature allowed?
quote: if hot water is accessible to the children, a thermostat must control it so that the water temperature is no higher than 120 degrees Fahrenheit
notes: Texas does not require hot water for hand washing; the 120°F cap applies only if hot water is accessible to children, and must be thermostat-controlled.

question: What must a licensed child-care center in Texas obtain before administering a medication to a child in its care?
answer: Authorization from the child's parent: in writing (signed and dated), in an electronic format that can be viewed and saved, or by telephone for a single dose
quote: Authorization to administer medication to a child in your care must be obtained from the child’s parent: (1) In writing, signed and dated [Medium-High]; (2) In an electronic format that is capable of being viewed and saved [Medium-High]; or (3) By telephone to administer a single dose of a medication.
notes: Authorization expires on the first anniversary of the date it is given (§746.3803(b)). Not required to give medication in a medical emergency to prevent death or serious bodily injury (§746.3803(d)).

question: How often must a licensed child-care center in Texas practice a fire drill?
quote: You must practice a fire drill every month. The children must be able to safely exit the building within three minutes
notes: Children must be able to exit within three minutes. Severe-weather sheltering drills and lock-down drills are required at least four times a calendar year (§746.5205(2)-(3)).

question: How long must a licensed child-care center in Texas keep its medication administration records?
quote: You must keep all medication records for at least three months after administering the medication.
notes: Record named: medication records (child's name, medication, date/time/amount, employee who gave it).

question: In what position must an infant be placed for sleep at a licensed child-care center in Texas, absent a medical exception?
answer: Face-up (on the back), in the infant's own crib
quote: You must place an infant in a face-up sleeping position in the infant's own crib, unless you have a completed Sleep Exception Form that includes a signed statement from a health-care professional stating that a different sleeping position for the child is medically necessary
notes: 'Face-up' means on the back. Exception only with a completed Sleep Exception Form signed by a health-care professional. An infant who can roll over may do so after being placed face-up (§746.2427(b)).

question: How soon must a licensed child-care center in Texas notify Licensing (HHSC Child Care Regulation) after a child in care is injured and the injury requires medical treatment by a health-care professional or hospitalization?
unit: days (as soon as possible, no later than)
quote: You must notify us as soon as possible, but no later than two days after: (1) Any occurrence that renders all or part of your center unsafe or unsanitary for a child [Medium-High]; (2) Injury to a child in your care that requires medical treatment by a health-care professional or hospitalization
notes: Deadline to the licensing agency. Parents must be notified immediately after such an injury (§746.307(b)(1)); Licensing must be notified immediately if a child dies in care (§746.305(b)).

question: By when must a child enrolling at a licensed child-care center in Texas have completed the immunizations required for the child's age?
quote: All immunizations required for the child's age must be completed by the date of admission, unless:
notes: Exceptions: an exemption or exception verified by the date of admission, or a homeless child or child in foster care provisionally admitted for up to 30 days when evidence of immunization is not available (§746.613(c)(1)-(2)). Date of admission = first day the child is physically present (§746.123(4)).

question: Which staff at a licensed child-care center in Texas must hold a current certificate in pediatric CPR, and what minimum CPR coverage must be on the premises while children are in care?
answer: Each caregiver and the child-care center director; at least one employee or caregiver with current pediatric CPR must be on the premises while children are in care
quote: Each caregiver and the child-care center director must have a current certificate of training with an expiration or renewal date in pediatric cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). ... the operation must have at least one employee or caregiver on the premises while children are in care that has a current certificate in pediatric CPR.
notes: A new caregiver need not have pediatric CPR before unsupervised access, but one CPR-certified person must be on site. Each caregiver and the director must also hold current pediatric first aid (§746.1315(a)).

question: How far apart must cribs be placed in the infant care area of a licensed child-care center in Texas?
answer: No set distance: far enough apart that one infant may not reach into another crib
quote: The room arrangement of the infant care area must: ... Have cribs far enough apart so that one infant may not reach into another crib
notes: Texas sets no numeric crib spacing. Caregivers must also have enough space to walk and work between cribs, cots, and mats (§746.2403(5), §746.2909(3)).

question: Under Texas's Minimum Standards for Child-Care Centers (26 TAC Ch. 746), when does a child-care center's permit stop being valid?
answer: It has no fixed term: it remains valid through the renewal process and becomes invalid only when the center voluntarily closes or must close because of an enforcement action
quote: Permit is no longer valid--For purposes of this chapter, a permit remains valid through the renewal process. A permit only becomes invalid when your center voluntarily closes or must close because of an enforcement action
notes: Ch. 746 states no license term or renewal interval; this definition is the only statement of permit validity in the rulebook.

question: In Texas, on a field trip where children from a licensed child-care center mix with children and adults who are not from the center (e.g., a skating rink or amusement park), how many children may one caregiver supervise when the youngest child in the group is 4 years old?
quote: When children are on a field trip and are mixing with children and adults who are not from your child-care center ... If the age of the youngest child in the group is… Then you must have (number of caregivers) caregivers to supervise… Every (number of children) children ... 4 years 1 8
notes: Based on the youngest child, not the specified age; stricter than the classroom ratio (1:18). Adult volunteers or non-qualified employees may count toward this ratio only if the classroom ratio is met by qualified caregivers (§746.1801(b)). Trips to enclosed, controlled areas use the classroom ratio (§746.1801(c)).

question: In a Texas child-care center licensed for 13 or more children, with 13 or more children in care, by what percentage may the child/caregiver ratio for children 18 months and older be reduced during naptime when the rule's conditions are met?
quote: If 13 or more children are in care, you may reduce the child/caregiver ratio for children 18 months and older by 50% during naptime under the following conditions
notes: Conditions: groups combined in a central sleeping location, additional employees present in the building per the chart, caregivers physically in the napping room. Not available for children under 18 months.

question: In a Texas child-care center licensed for 13 or more children, with 13 or more children in care, during the 45 minutes after opening and the 45 minutes before closing, how many children 18 months and older may be grouped with one caregiver?
quote: When 13 or more children are in care, children who are 18 months and older may be grouped at a ratio of one caregiver per group of 16 children during the 45 minutes after opening and 45 minutes before closing.
notes: Not allowed for children younger than 18 months, and not allowed when 12 or fewer children are in care (§746.1709).

question: In a Texas child-care center licensed for 13 or more children, with 13 or more children in care, for at most how many minutes may groups of children 18 months through four years be mixed for a joint activity that exceeds the maximum group size (other than meals, field trips, outdoor play and naptime)?
quote: When 13 or more children are in care, you may mix groups for joint activities and exceed the maximum group size for limited times under the following conditions: (1) For children 18 months through four years, for a maximum of 30 minutes
notes: Children five and older: up to 1 1/2 hours; meals, field trips, outdoor play and naptime: the length of the activity. The child/caregiver ratio must still be met (§746.1611(b)).

question: In Texas, can a licensed child-care center ever count a 16- or 17-year-old employee who has a high school diploma in the child/caregiver ratio?
quote: You may employ a 16 or 17 year old who has a high school diploma or its equivalent and count the person in the child/caregiver ratio, provided that: (1) You don't leave the person alone with sole responsibility
notes: Only if the person is never left alone with sole responsibility, works in the same room supervised by a qualified caregiver, and completed an approved child-care-related career program. The general caregiver minimum age is 18 (§746.1107).
